title: The simplicial relative join
statement:
Use simplicial sets, standard simplices, products and degreewise pullbacks from [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones], and joins and join cones from [def-coef-infinity-relative-cone]. All objects are small in the fixed sufficiently large universe. Given simplicial maps $f:A\to C$ and $g:B\to C$, define the relative join by
$$A\star_C B=(A\star B)\times_{C\star C}(\Delta^1\times C).$$
Here $f\star g$ sends each join summand $A_i\times B_j$ to $C_i\times C_j$ by $(a,b)\mapsto(f(a),g(b))$, with the unique map on a formal degree $-1$ factor. The other pullback map $\rho_C:\Delta^1\times C\to C\star C$ sends $(\epsilon,\sigma)$ in degree $n$, where $\epsilon:[n]\to[1]$ is monotone and $\sigma\in C_n$, to the join summand with initial block $\epsilon^{-1}(0)$ and final block $\epsilon^{-1}(1)$, using the restrictions of $\sigma$ to those blocks. An empty block uses the unique formal degree $-1$ element. Thus an $n$-simplex of the relative join is a pair $(z,(\epsilon,\sigma))$ satisfying $(f\star g)(z)=\rho_C(\epsilon,\sigma)$. For a monotone $\alpha:[m]\to[n]$, its simplicial operator is
$$(z,(\epsilon,\sigma))\longmapsto(\alpha^*z,(\epsilon\alpha,\alpha^*\sigma)).$$

Write $p_C:A\star_C B\to C$ for $(z,(\epsilon,\sigma))\mapsto\sigma$. If $\iota_A:A\to A\star B$ and $\iota_B:B\to A\star B$ are the pure-factor inclusions, the relative-join inclusions are
$$i_A(a)=(\iota_A(a),(0,f(a))),\qquad i_B(b)=(\iota_B(b),(1,g(b))),$$
where $0,1:[n]\to[1]$ are the constant parameters in degree $n$.
Given also simplicial maps $f':A'\to C'$ and $g':B'\to C'$, and simplicial maps $a:A\to A'$, $b:B\to B'$, $h:C\to C'$ with $f'a=hf$ and $g'b=hg$, the induced relative-join map is
$$(z,(\epsilon,\sigma))\longmapsto((a\star b)(z),(\epsilon,h(\sigma))).$$
When both maps $C\to C$ are identities, identify $C\star_C C$ with $\Delta^1\times C$ by the second pullback projection; its inverse is $(\epsilon,\sigma)\mapsto(\rho_C(\epsilon,\sigma),(\epsilon,\sigma))$.

For a simplicial map $u:A\to C$ and a vertex $c\in C_0$, let $\{c\}$ mean the copy of $\Delta^0$ mapping constantly to $c$, and put $A_c=A\times_C\{c\}$. The fiber-cone map
$$j_c:A_c^{\triangleright}=A_c\star\Delta^0\longrightarrow A\star_C C$$
sends $w$ in degree $n$, with join-block parameter $\epsilon$, to $((r\star c)(w),(\epsilon,c_n))$, where $r:A_c\to A$ is the pullback projection, $c:\Delta^0\to C$ is the vertex map and $c_n$ its degenerate $n$-simplex. These formulas specify data only, with no quasicategory or universal-cone assertion.
